header.name: Behavioural Economics
header.description: The course will provide a theoretical understanding of behavioural economics, and then apply these theories to do experimental analysis in a laboratory setting. Behavioural economics incorporates human traits of cognition, social preferences, and emotional responses to better understand choices made in a setting that may not seem "rational" in the traditional sense of the word. Understanding of choices influenced by behaviour is useful in a variety of arenas, including policy making, IO, and finance. Behavioural economics literature also has inter- disciplinary relevance with psychology and cognitive sciences.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Identify how individuals influenced by behavioural biases behave differently from perfectly rational agents

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Explaining the relevance of risk, uncertainty and time in individual decisions.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Determining the role of social preferences and strategic settings to decision making

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Implementing these theories to experimental economics, policy, decisions by firms, and decisions made in financial markets

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Designing lab experiments that help to identify the presence and estimate the extent of such behavioural biases, specifically to be coded on

lecture_topics: Decision Making in Economics under Certainty
Intertemporal Choice (Procrastination, Hyperbolic Discounting, and Present Bias)
Human Sociality (Altruism, Inequity Aversion, Conformity, Reciprocity, Fairness, Vengeance)

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Design of Lab Experiments (Question, Idea, and Coding)

lecture_topics: Brief Introduction to Behavioural Finance and Neuroeconomics

assessments.type_label: Design of Lab Experiments (Question, Idea, and Coding)
